Notice of Funding Opportunity, Part 1 
1.  Funding Details 
Multiple Topic Areas 
Approximate total available funding for all topic areas:  $237,000,000 in fiscal year 2027   
 
Topic Area 1: Refurbishment and Reuse of Critical Grid Equipment 
• Approximate total available funding:  $50,000,000 
• Approximate number of awards:  3–20 
• Approximate dollar amount of individual awards:  $2,500,000–$15,000,000 
• Minimum cost share required:  50% 
• Approximate award project period:  up to 24 months  
• Anticipated length of budget periods:  up to 24 months  
• Anticipated number of budget periods:  1 
Topic Area 2: Alternative Materials and Subcomponents 
• Approximate total available funding:  $187,000,000 
• Approximate number of awards:  7–50 
• Approximate dollar amount of individual awards:  $1,000,000–$25,000,000 
• Minimum cost share required:  50% 
• Approximate award project period:  up to 48 months  
• Anticipated number of budget periods:  1 
• Anticipated length of budget periods:  Phase 1—up to 12 months. Phase 2—up to 36 
months  
2.  Period of Performance 
DOE anticipates both Topic Areas will be coextensive (singular budget period); however, 
Topic Area Two (2) will contain two Phases.  For Topic Area 2, Phase 2 will be contingent on a 
Go/No-Go decision point.  You can find a complete list of post-award requirements and more 
information on the Go/No-Go review in NOFO Part 2, Award Administration Information. 
B.  Executive Summary 
The Department of Energy (DOE), Office of Electricity (OE), is launching a strategic 
grid supply chain program, as appropriated in the Energy and Water Development and Related 
Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026 (Pub. L. No. 119-74, Div. B), designed to significantly 
enhance the domestic supply chain for critical electric grid components such as (but not limited 
to) distribution transformers, larger power transformers, circuit breakers, switchgear, reclosers, 
insulators, busbars, and high-voltage bushings.  This program seeks to (1) bolster domestic 
capabilities and capacity to handle supply chain shocks, (2) complement ongoing investments in 
domestic manufacturing capacity to meet increased equipment demands, and (3) strengthen 
supply chains for next-generation grid components that reduce demand for existing solutions and 
enable global dominance.
